classification.difficultyReason: Introduce a perpendicular projection or use equal gradients to connect the unit-circle radius with the tangent-line triangle, then interpret its unit horizontal run.

inlines.text: Show that the number of the radial projection on the tangent number line is equal to the gradient of the radius, i.e.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, question 104 figure between subtitle and proof instruction.
spec.description: Unshaded unit circle with double-arrowed coordinate axes and a separate double-arrowed vertical tangent number line at horizontal coordinate 1. A radius reaches a marked first-quadrant circle point, then continues as a dotted line to a marked tangent projection. An angle arc is labelled theta. A brace from tangent value 0 to the projection is labelled t. This intentionally replaces the source brace variable x to distinguish the projection value from the horizontal coordinate.
spec.mathematics: The radius point is (cos theta, sin theta). Its collinear projection onto horizontal coordinate 1 is (1, tan theta). The drawing parameter only determines an illustrative first-quadrant orientation. The tangent number-line scale is the same as the coordinate-axis scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Preserve the supplied angle and numerical number-line labels. Rename only the source brace variable x to t. Do not label the projection with tan theta or add solution-only triangle names, projection guides or equations.

inlines.text: Similar right triangles give the same rise-to-run ratio. The projected triangle has horizontal run 1, so its rise is the gradient of the radius.

answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the circle's centre, $A$ the marked point on the circle, $Q$ its radial projection on the tangent number line, and $B$ the point where that line meets the horizontal axis. Let $H$ be the perpendicular projection of $A$ onto the horizontal axis.

The right triangles $\triangle OHA$ and $\triangle OBQ$ share the angle $\theta$ at $O$, so they are similar. Here $OB=1$, $BQ=t$, $OH=\cos\theta$ and $AH=\sin\theta$. Therefore,

$$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{BQ}{OB}\\t&=\frac{AH}{OH}\\t&=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\\t&=\tan\theta.\end{align*}$$

The ratio $\frac{AH}{OH}$ is also the gradient of the radius. Hence the tangent number-line value equals that gradient.
